jobDescription: A national home-and-garden retailer is refitting 40 of its stores over the next three years while they keep trading. The Project Manager, Store Refit Programme, builds integrated schedules, manages the main contractors through progress meetings, variations and disputes, controls each refit budget against the approved capital spend and works with store trading teams so that customers can keep shopping during the works. A recognised project management certification is required. Each refit is let to a main contractor under a standard building contract, with variations above a set value referred to the commercial manager, and disputes over delay or quality are expected to be settled at site level wherever possible. The role reports to the head of store development and works alongside two other refit project managers.
requirements: Builds and maintains integrated programme schedules for store refits.
Manages main contractors, resolves programme disputes and handles contract variations.
Controls refit budgets and reports variances to the property director.
Coordinates store trading teams so that refits run with minimum disruption to customers.
Holds a recognised project management certification.

evidence.text: Project manager in the store development team at Brackley Home & Garden, July 2020 to present, running refits of stores between 30,000 and 60,000 square feet.
Built the integrated refit schedules in the planning tool, linking strip-out, mechanical and electrical works, fixture installation and stock replenishment.
Tracked each refit budget against the approved capital spend and reported monthly variances to the property director, with commentary on change orders.

Agreed overnight and weekend working windows with store managers so that customer areas stayed open during the works, and issued a weekly works notice to each store listing the areas closed and the hoarding positions.
Attended weekly progress meetings with the main contractors, kept the meeting actions list and logged their variation requests for the commercial manager to assess.
Work sample: an anonymised refit schedule for one store, showing the 11-week programme, the critical path through mechanical and electrical works and the stock replenishment plan for reopening.
Interviewer impression (panel round): a born leader with real gravitas; I would expect contractors to fall in line behind them without much pushback.

Recruiter verification note: the candidate's PRINCE2 Practitioner certificate was checked on the accrediting body's successful-candidate register; it is listed as current, with the examination recorded in May 2022.

propositions.text: The candidate built integrated refit schedules linking strip-out, mechanical and electrical works, fixture installation and stock replenishment.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the schedules and the work sample shows one store's programme and critical path.

propositions.text: The candidate holds a PRINCE2 Practitioner certificate listed as current on the accrediting body's register.
propositions.rationale: The recruiter verification note records the register check.

propositions.text: The candidate is a born leader whose gravitas brings main contractors into line during refit disputes.
propositions.rationale: The panel remark is an impression plus a speculation about how contractors would respond; it describes no dispute the candidate handled. The documented contractor work is attendance and logging of variation requests, so the impression cannot be converted into a conclusion about contractor management.

gold.expectedGap: The candidate attended contractor progress meetings and logged variation requests, but no source shows them resolving a dispute or deciding a variation.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Record the panel impression under interview signal risks with its source; keep the scheduling, budget and certification evidence, and keep the contractor work at attendance and logging.
followUpTargets: Ask the candidate for an example of a contractor dispute or variation they handled personally, what they decided and how it was recorded.
